newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Yen,Swiss franc up in slow Hungary FX futures mkt.
newsitem.headline: Yen,Swiss franc up in slow Hungary FX futures mkt.

text.p: Hungarian currency futures trade on Tuesday was low, with the Budapest Commodities Exchange (BCE) recording 1.96 billion forints and the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) ending tradeless.
The Swiss franc and the Japanese yen were the most popular currencies on the BCE, accounting between them for two-thirds of the total 13,297 lots traded.
"These two currencies are preferred for selling," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
"The Swiss and Japanese interest rates are so much lower than the difference between the forint devaluation and the Hungarian interest rates that they give a good hedging possibility," he said.

Herczeg said selling forward can bring an interest rate return but has its risk. "The risks are that the dollar cross rates rise too much or that the forint weakens within the 4.5 percent intervention range," he said.
Prices for the Swiss franc rose for March by 10 fillers to 120.10 forints and for September by 40 fillers to 130.7 forints.
The December yen rose by 48 fillers to 174.20 forints per 100 yen.
Herczeg said that the last few days have seen a corrective phase to recent dollar trends but the U.S. unit is in demand again.
"There is a bullish sentiment to the dollar with people taking long positions," he said.
Both March and December dollars rose 45 fillers to 176.00 and 193.25 respectively.
There was no trade on the BSE for the second day running with the only price movement registered in the June Ecu, which fell 1.67 forints to 210.05.
